claim: AWS RAM shares resources across AWS accounts, within an organization or its OUs, and, for supported resource types, with IAM roles and IAM users.
question: Who can resources be shared with in AWS RAM?

values.display: share your resources across AWS accounts
with IAM roles and IAM users for supported resource types

evidence.quote: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) helps you securely share your resources across AWS accounts, within your organization or organizational units (OUs) in AWS Organizations, and with IAM roles and IAM users for supported resource types.

claim: Sharing a resource with AWS RAM removes the need to provision and manage that resource in every account.
question: Why share a resource with AWS RAM instead of creating it in every account?

values.display: eliminates the need to provision and manage resources in every account

evidence.quote: You can use AWS RAM to share resources with other AWS accounts. This eliminates the need to provision and manage resources in every account.

claim: When a resource is shared with another account, that account gets access to the resource, and the policies and permissions in that account apply to the shared resource.
question: Whose policies apply to a resource shared through AWS RAM?

values.display: any policies and permissions in that account apply

evidence.quote: When you share a resource with another account, that account is granted access to the resource and any policies and permissions in that account apply to the shared resource.

claim: AWS RAM can share with any AWS account; sharing with OUs or the whole organization is possible when sharing within the organization is enabled.
question: When can AWS RAM share with an OU or a whole organization?

values.display: You can share resources with any AWS account.
sharing within your organization is enabled

evidence.quote: You can share resources with any AWS account. If you are part of an organization in AWS Organizations and sharing within your organization is enabled, you can also share resources with OUs or your entire organization.

claim: AWS RAM can share with IAM roles and IAM users only for supported resource types.
question: Can AWS RAM share a resource with an IAM role or user?

values.display: For supported resource types

evidence.quote: For supported resource types, you can also share resources with IAM roles and IAM users.

claim: Accounts outside your organization receive an invitation to join a resource share, and they can use the shared resources only after they accept it.
question: What happens when you share a resource with an account outside your organization?

values.display: receive an invitation to join the resource share

evidence.quote: If you share resources with accounts that are outside of your organization, those accounts receive an invitation to join the resource share. After they accept the invitation, they can start using the shared resources.

claim: Resources shared with an account also appear in the console pages and the List and Describe APIs of their resource type, next to the account's own resources.
question: Where does a consumer account see resources shared with it?

values.display: respective List/Describe APIs for those resource types

evidence.quote: The resources that are shared with your account also appear in the respective resource console pages and the respective List/Describe APIs for those resource types.

claim: An account controls access to resources shared with it by using IAM policies.
question: How can an account control access to resources shared with it through AWS RAM?

values.display: You can specify IAM policies

evidence.quote: You can specify IAM policies to control access to resources shared with you.

claim: You can stop sharing a resource by removing it from the resource share or by deleting the resource share.
question: How do you stop sharing a resource in AWS RAM?

values.display: removing it from the resource share
deleting the resource share

evidence.quote: Yes, you can stop sharing a resource by removing it from the resource share or by deleting the resource share.

claim: All AWS RAM API calls are logged in AWS CloudTrail, and events are sent whenever resource shares change.
question: How are changes to AWS RAM resource shares monitored?

values.display: logged in AWS CloudTrail
triggered whenever there are changes to resource shares

evidence.quote: All calls to AWS RAM APIs are logged in AWS CloudTrail. In addition, Amazon CloudWatch Events are triggered whenever there are changes to resource shares.

note: The FAQ uses the former name Amazon CloudWatch Events; the current name is Amazon EventBridge (RULINGS rule 6). Writers should say EventBridge and ground the name in the RAM user guide if needed.

claim: AWS managed permissions are created and maintained by AWS, and every resource type has a default AWS managed permission.
question: What is an AWS managed permission in AWS RAM?

values.display: created and maintained by AWS
Every resource type has a default AWS managed permission.

qualifiers.scope: per resource type in a resource share

evidence.quote: AWS managed permissions are created and maintained by AWS and grant permissions for many common customer scenarios. Every resource type has a default AWS managed permission.

claim: Customer managed permissions are permissions you write and maintain, stating who can do what under which conditions on shared resources, so you can grant least privilege.
question: When do you use a customer managed permission in AWS RAM?

values.display: permissions that you author and maintain
follow the best practice of least privilege

evidence.quote: Customer managed permissions are permissions that you author and maintain by precisely specifying who can do what under which conditions with resources shared using AWS RAM.
You can follow the best practice of least privilege, granting only the permissions required to perform tasks on shared resources.

claim: A managed permission defines the actions, conditions and principals for a resource type in a resource share, and each resource type is associated with either an AWS managed or a customer managed permission.
question: What does a managed permission define in AWS RAM?

values.display: either an AWS managed permission or a customer managed permission

evidence.quote: A managed permission defines which actions can be performed, under which conditions, and by which principals for supported resource types in a resource share. You can associate either an AWS managed permission or a customer managed permission with each resource type in a resource share using AWS RAM.

claim: Sharing resources with AWS RAM has no additional cost.
question: Does sharing resources with AWS RAM cost anything?

values.display: share resources at no additional cost

evidence.quote: No. You can share resources at no additional cost.

claim: To share with AWS RAM, you add resources to a resource share, choose a managed permission for each resource type, and specify who gets access.
question: What are the parts of an AWS RAM resource share?

values.display: choosing a managed permission to associate with each resource type

evidence.quote: You can easily share resources by adding resources to a resource share, choosing a managed permission to associate with each resource type, and specifying whom you want to have access to the resources.
